Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Financial Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I will now turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Financial Group's results for the Q3 2024. With me this morning are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Wong, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; Amanda Lee, Chief Marketing Officer; and Thomas Berger, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Financial Group delivered record results in the Q3 2024, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on sustaining strong revenue growth, driving operational efficiency, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand reputation, promoting a diverse and inclusive culture, and delivering superior returns to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key areas driving our performance. Non-interest income showed remarkable resilience, reaching $2.4 billion, up 18% year-over-year, thanks to diversified fee streams amid volatile markets. Our asset sensitivity position remains modestly positive, supporting NII in this rate environment. We've made significant progress on our efficiency ratio, hitting 61.2% with ambitious targets ahead. Capital returns are robust, with increased dividends and ongoing buybacks. Deposit costs are managed amid competition, loan growth outlook is steady at 4-5%, segmented loan expansion is strong across commercial, consumer, and mortgage portfolios, and operating expenses are controlled with clear drivers.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, John, and good morning. UniBank Financial Group reported net income of $2.8 billion for the Q3 2024, or $1.85 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 12% year-over-year, driven by growth in our loan portfolio and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income was exceptionally strong at $2.4 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, exceeding internal expectations and highlighting the resilience of our diversified fee-based revenue streams in a choppy macroeconomic environment. Now representing 32% of total revenue, up from 28% a year ago, this reflects our strategic shift toward stable, recurring sources in a higher-for-longer interest rate world. We saw broad strength across segments, with elevated volatility—the VIX averaging 22 in Q3 versus 16 last year—boosting capital markets and trading, while robust equity markets, including an 8% S&P 500 gain, lifted investment banking fees. Softer FX volatility and normalizing credit card spending provided some offsets.

In capital markets and advisory fees, we hit $850 million, up 32% year-over-year, our top performer, propelled by surging M&A and ECM activity. Global M&A volumes reached $1.1 trillion per Dealogic, the strongest since Q4 2021, driven by pent-up demand and consolidations in tech and healthcare. We advised on 15 deals over $1 billion, including a $12 billion mid-cap fintech merger echoing Plaid-Visa dynamics, and led bookruns on three IPOs totaling $4.2 billion, riding the wave from Arm Holdings' listing. Debt capital markets thrived with high-yield issuance up 25% amid refinancing ahead of SOFR-linked maturities; our U.S. investment-grade underwriting market share rose to 7.2% from 6.1% per Bloomberg, aided by deep renewables coverage like $2.5 billion in green bonds for NextEra Energy-like clients.

North America drove 65% of growth, with U.S. megadeals rebounding. EMEA grew 12% despite UK gilt crisis echoes and ECB hikes limiting leveraged buyouts, strong in European industrials. APAC surged 45%, anchored by China's stimulus and partnerships like DBS for cross-border ECM.

Trading revenues reached $620 million, up 22% year-over-year. FICC, 55% of this, benefited from rate volatility post-Fed's hike to 5.25-5.50%, with macro trading capturing $180 million from shorting long-end duration ahead of pivot signals, and credit trading on HY spread widening like 2022 energy plays. Equities trading added $220 million, prime brokerage up 15% on AI-hyped hedge fund balances. Our proprietary algo suite, enhanced by ML models from LSEG data, cut execution slippage by 12 basis points. U.S. Treasuries volatility spiked to 120% annualized, JPY carry unwinds yielded $45 million FX flows; VaR averaged $35 million daily, flat quarter-over-quarter.

Wealth and asset management fees were $520 million, up 12% year-over-year, with AUM at $1.8 trillion, up 11%, from $120 billion net new money—60% HNWIs via Pinnacle private banking. Equity, fixed income, and alternatives each contributed 7%, 2%, and 2%; evergreen private credit funds at 9-11% net IRR drew $25 billion amid loan compression. U.S. HNWIs favored sustainable mandates up 20%, Europe de-risked amid energy issues, Asia grew 25% via Temasek UHNW ties.

Service charges and cards hit $280 million, up 8% year-over-year but flat sequentially as spending slowed to 2.5% real. Interchange grew 10% with 4 million new neo-bank accounts; deposit charges dipped 2% from fee waivers but offset by treasury upsell, cross-sell at 3.8x via SME APIs. Other income, including bancassurance JV premiums, added $130 million up 9%.

These results affirm our Fee 3.0 framework digitizing fees at scale, with $250 million YTD tech spend including GenAI for wealth advice, cutting advisor time 30% and lifting conversions 15%. Blockchain trade finance processed $15 billion, 2% APAC share per SWIFT. We expect 10-12% Q4 growth assuming VIX 18-20, S&P EPS 6%; risks like U.S. shutdown or China property mitigated by 40/30/30 diversification targeting 14% RoTE. ESG in 25% mandates aligns with regulations. Q3 buybacks of $1 billion partly funded here, $8 billion authorized remaining. We are generating strong returns on equity and committed to shareholder value.

Turning to asset sensitivity and interest rate risk management, a cornerstone of our balance sheet resilience amid rate volatility since the Fed's 2023 peak. Our ALM framework optimizes NII sensitivity while safeguarding EVE across scenarios, using proprietary IRRBB models compliant with Basel III, CECL, IFRS 9, with 10,000+ stochastic SOFR paths calibrated to GFC and tightening history.

At quarter-end, we're modestly asset-sensitive: +100 bps parallel shock yields +$185 million NII@R, or +2.1% of base, up from +$160 million last quarter on $450 billion commercial loans repricing at 65% SOFR/prime—better than neutral peers like JPMorgan, BofA. +200 bps EVE -4.8%, within -10% limit, improved from -5.9%. -100 bps is -$120 million, buffered by deposits.

Shift from pre-2022 liability-sensitive via loan repricing (C&I 40% loans at 85% beta, NII $2.8 billion up 12%), deposit betas at 38% overall (24% NMDs, 55% of $1.2 trillion base, below 45% FDIC avg via Deposit Shield up 8%), wholesale 12% at 92% capped by FHLB at 4.85%. U.S. 85% assets at 3.25% NIM, Europe $120 billion at 2.85% Euribor 72%, APAC $80 billion 70% floating HKD/USD hedging Fed.

Risk tools: $35 billion IRS/SOFR futures, net DV01 -$15 million locking 4.2% on 2021-22 mortgages (98% SOFR post-LIBOR). Duration gap +0.15 years (assets 2.8, liabilities 2.65), $10 billion Treasury options. Phase II AI-ALM with Moody's AXIS/GenAI boosts deposit runoff forecasts 22%, climate paths per NGFS. Limits: NII@R <5%, EVE <8%, daily hedging.

Forward, adding agency MBS ($50 billion at 4.6%), ARMs to 30%; NIM 3.45% eyes 5-7% 2025 loan growth. Cumulative $650 million NII uplift since Q3 2022 supports 12%+ ROTE 2025.

On efficiency ratio, calculated as adjusted non-interest expense over total revenue, ours improved to 61.2%, 380 bps better quarter-over-quarter from 65.0% Q4 2023, 420 bps vs. Q1 2023—best Q1 in five years, revenue outpacing expenses 2.8x under Efficiency Edge since 2022. FY 2023 at 63.1% beat 64-65% guide.

Consumer/Business Banking (55% revenue) at 59.8%, NIM 3.65% up from 3.25%, digital deposits +28% via UniMobile Zelle/AI fraud (costs -22%), 45 branch closures offset by Walmart/Target embedded finance $145 million fees. Commercial/Corporate (30%) 64.5% with Basel IV drag but 15% middle-market lending $12.5 billion, RPA -18% costs, UniCash Pro 72% adoption. Wealth/Investment 58.2% from $4.2 billion robo-advisory inflows via Aladdin.

U.S. (80% $28 billion revenue) 60.1%, deposit betas 22%; Europe 65.8% MiFID II/PSD2 offsets; APAC 62.4% Finacle digital loans $2.1 billion SMEs.

Initiatives: 65% cloud AWS/Azure $180 million savings, peak 45 million txns +32%; ML onboarding 85% -5 days to 45 min, NPL provisions -14%; ZBB opex -9% to $4.2 billion.

FY 2024 target 57-59%, Q2 60.5%; 2026 sub-55% like Wells/BofA peers, 60%+ earnings returns at 4.2% yield.

Capital returns: ROTCE 14.2% up 120 bps, CET1 12.8% exceeds 11-13% cycle target, affirmed DFAST (420 bps depletion adverse). Q3 dividend $1.20/share +10% YoY, payout 38% < peers; announce +12.5% to $1.35/share December, annualized $5.40, 3.1% yield, 8-10% growth goal.

YTD buybacks 45 million shares 3.2% float at $162 avg, $7.3 billion ($2.1 billion Q3 10b5-1), $10 billion remaining of $15 billion auth. TBVPS +$4.20 to $148.50, EPS +5%.

Framework: regulatory > growth > returns, 50/50 dividends/buybacks post-11.5% CET1. U.S. 65% RWA buybacks 2.8%, Midwest C&I 16% ROTCE; Europe CET1 13.2% €500 million UK IB; APAC conservative wealth +12%.

2025 $12-14 billion returns: $5.4 billion dividends, $7-9 billion buybacks >12% CET1; 4-5% EPS, NIM 3.55%+, fees via BNPL Visa. CECL 1.15%, 25 bps office CRE.

Deposit costs averaged 2.82% up 58 bps QoQ/142 bps YoY on Fed 5.33%, NIM +12 bps to 3.45%. DDA 38% at 12 bps stable commercial; interest-bearing 42% 2.45% (+65 bps) MMDAs 3.12%; CDs 20% 4.68% (+72 bps) retail surge.

Beta 48% tracks PNC/Regions < Truist, lag retail/commercial <30%. Competition: Ally/SoFi 4.50-5.25% vs. our 3.75%, MMFs 5.2-5.4% $1.2 trillion flows. Midwest +52 bps 2.65% sticky 82% LDR; Southeast +68 bps 3.05%.

AI dynamic pricing FIS cuts beta 8%, Elite Rewards 2.25% APY cashback 15% inflows; commercial Treasury 0.85% +22%. Target 40% non-interest via OneBank 2.5 million users 65% digital; cap brokered 10%, ICS/CDARS. Q4 costs ~3.10% +20-30 bps, NIM trough Q1 +15-20 bps H1; HQLA 125%.

Loan growth outlook 4-5% FY 2024, 5-7% 2025 selective high-return. C&I 5-6% middle-market capex/onshoring, utilization 52% +150 bps, Southeast 12% <$50 million share, APAC trade +8% HSBC. CRE flat 2024/1-2% 2025, office 8% de-risked, industrial/retail +4%, Sunbelt multifamily watch LTV>85% 15%. Consumer 6-7%, auto +9% $2.5 billion FICO 740 Ally, HELOC +12%; mortgages flat 1% 6.8% rates, digital 85% pull-through Fannie 6.2% refi.

AI decisioning -40% times +25 bps returns, $500 million green loans IRA. NCOs 40-50 bps FY/45-55 bps 2025, DQs 1.15%/consumer 2.1% <2.8% FDIC. PCL $180 million Q3/YTD $650 million 0.65%, FY $750-800 million 1.45x coverage CECL soft landing 85% prob GDP 2.1%/U 4.2%. C&I DQs 0.8% IG sponsors, CRE criticized 4.2% office reserves 250 bps NCO<20 bps, cards 3.5% Plaid skips. Southeast NCO 30 bps, Midwest 1.8% overlays cap>7%.

Loan growth details: total +7.2% YoY $285 billion, 11th sequential, adj +8.4% ex non-core CRE >5.1% peers FDIC. Commercial 52% $148 billion +9.8% seq 2.1%, C&I $92 billion +12.5% utilization 48% capex supply chain GDPNow 2.8%; Southeast 14% data/logistics, Midwest 6% ISM<50. CRE $56 billion +5.2% multifamily/industrial 65% office 15% SOFR+6.5%, DQs 0.42% reserves 1.15%. nCino/Moody's <48 hours 70% +22% conv, ESG $4.2 billion Sun Belt solar.

Consumer 28% $80 billion +6.1% seq 1.8% >4-6% guide savings 3.8%/U 3.8%. Auto $42 billion +9.2% inventory 2.7 million FICO 735 NCO 4.25%<4.8%, indirect 15%; personal $18 billion +4.8% refi, cards $20 billion +5.5% util 32% wages+4.1%. Sun Belt auto +8%, Northeast flat; AI Experian 92% subprime flag. Auto app Plaid +28% digital, cross-sell 45% deposits NIM 3.45%.

Mortgage 20% $57 billion +3.9% seq 1.2% >MBA 2.1%, HFS $1.2 billion GOS 125 bps. Refi -18% 7.1% rates 22% vol, purchase +22% $8.5 billion 97% LTV FHA. Jumbo +7% FL/CA +5% prices, gov 35% Rocket eff. Sun Belt +6%/Midwest +1%, DQs 0.28% reserves 1.42% Case-Shiller. Blend/Black Knight 85% e-close 14 days, Figure blockchain.

Guide Q4 comm 9-11%, cons 6-7%, mort 4-5% Fed 5.25-5.50; CET1 12.8% Basel endgame. ROE 12.5%, risks CRE maturities 85% floating $15 billion undrawn.

Operating expenses $2.48 billion +4.2% YoY flat FX, seq +1.8% seasonal, eff 57.8% +120 bps YoY in 55-60%, <JPM 58%/Wells 62%. Comp/benefits 42% $1.04B +6% headcount +1.2% 48,500 comp $212k +4.7% tech war offset RPA -12% back-office $45 million; H2 3-4% Coursera GenAI.

Tech/data 22% $546M +12% $1.2 billion FY: cloud 65% AWS/Azure $28 million mainframe to k8s; AI Palantir/Salesforce fraud -35% false pos cross-sell +18%; cyber $85 million zero incidents post-Change. Tech/revenue 8.2%<8.7%, ROI 15-20% 2026.

Occupancy/equip/prof 18% $446M +2%: occupancy $210M 85 branch close 15% network $32 million Midwest like BofA, ATM contactless +22% wallets; prof +5% $112M Basel IV/ESG CSRD.

Marketing/FDIC/other 18% $488M -1%: marketing $145M -7% digital Google/Meta ROAS 4.2x $4.2 billion deposits 2.1%; FDIC -8%. NA 65% flat Canada app 78%>65% JDP; Europe 20% +7% MiFID III/ring-fence €50M Frankfurt DORA; APAC 15% +11% India UPI/Singapore sandbox -2% FX.

FY opex +4-5%<6.2% McKinsey, +250 bps eff since 2022 ZBB TechFirst sub-55% 2026; risks infl 3.1% talent, tailwinds automation regs. EPS +10-12% embedded Visa.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility, commercial real estate exposures, cybersecurity threats, and geopolitical tensions. We are implementing enhanced controls and monitoring to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

David Wong:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with non-performing assets at 0.45% and net charge-offs at 0.35%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in AI-driven platforms and cloud infrastructure are yielding significant results.

Robert Kline:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes, optimizing our infrastructure, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making.

Amanda Lee:
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention.

Thomas Berger:
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star then one on your touchtone telephone. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Could you please provide more detail on the impact of market conditions on non-interest income?

John Reynolds:
Thanks, John. As Michael detailed, the volatility and equity gains really propelled capital markets and trading, with M&A and IPO activity exceeding expectations. Our diversification and tech investments like GenAI are key to sustaining this momentum.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mary Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mary Johnson:
What is your outlook for loan growth and credit quality?

Michael Chen:
Mary, we're guiding 4-5% for the year with pickup to 5-7% in 2025, focused on C&I and consumer while cautious on CRE. Credit metrics stay strong with low NCOs and solid reserves under CECL for a soft landing.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Can you discuss the impact of interest rate risks and asset sensitivity?

Lisa Patel:
Absolutely, David. Our modestly asset-sensitive position and hedging with swaps and options keep us resilient to shocks, as Michael outlined, with tech-enhanced modeling for real-time adjustments.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for technology investments going forward?

Elena Vasquez:
Emily, we're doubling down on AI for credit and personalization, cloud migrations delivering savings, and cybersecurity, all supporting efficiency and growth as evidenced by our origination speedups.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to John Reynolds for any closing remarks.

John Reynolds:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
